newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-REID TAKES ONE-STROKE LEAD INTO FINAL ROUND IN HAWAII.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-REID TAKES ONE-STROKE LEAD INTO FINAL ROUND IN HAWAII.

text.p: Mike Reid took a
one-stroke lead into the final round of the $1.2 million
Hawaiian Open golf tournament after a third-round 66 on
Saturday.
Paul Stankowski shot the day's low round of 64 to move
into second place, two strokes ahead of five other players,
including defending champion Jim Furyk, who had a 66, and
British Open champion Tom Lehman, with a 69.
Reid was the first-round leader after a 10 under par 62,
but stumbled with a second-round 72.
He had eight birdies and two bogeys on Saturday and sealed
the lead with a birdie tap-in on the par-five 18th hole. It's
the first time Reid has led a tournament after three rounds
since the 1989 PGA Championship, which he ended up losing.
Reid has struggled since injuring his right wrist four
years ago. His injury is behind him, but he has been unable to
find a set of clubs he likes, changing clubs four times in the
last four weeks.
He almost did not come to Hawaii, but realised that he was
more likely to find his game in competition than back at home
in Utah.
"You can only improve so much putting on the carpet and
hitting off the deck into a snowbank," said Reid.
Stankowski had the most volatile round of the day, as well
as the lowest.
He began with an eagle on the first hole on a three-foot
putt and then pitched in from 60 feet for another eagle on the
18th hole. In between Stankowski had eight birdies, four
bogeys and just four pars.
